paper.title: Fairness and Privacy Guarantees in Federated Contextual Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Federated contextual bandit with fairness of exposure (non-private)
unmapped: Objective is fairness regret: sum over rounds of L1 distance between learner's policy and merit-proportional (fairness-of-exposure) optimal policy, averaged over agents
Agents know merit functions f^i with minimum merit gamma and Lipschitz constant L
Each of m agents observes its own context set each round; shared parameter theta*
settings.definition_quote: We abstract the problem as a federated contextual bandit setting where each of M=[m] agents are learning about actions a in D. ... y_t^i(a_t^i) = theta^* . x_t^i(a_t^i) + eta_t(a_t^i) ... For agent i at round t the instantaneous fairness regret is defined as FR_t^i = sum_a |pi_*^i(a, X_t^i) - pi_t^i(a, X_t^i)|.

settings.name_in_paper: Federated contextual bandit with fairness of exposure and federated differential privacy
unmapped: Objective is fairness regret against merit-proportional optimal policy, averaged over agents
(epsilon, delta, m)-federated differential privacy under continual multi-agent observation
Agents know merit functions with minimum merit gamma and Lipschitz constant L
settings.definition_quote: a randomized multi-agent contextual bandit algorithm A = (A^i)_{i=1}^m is (epsilon,delta, m)-federated differentially private under continual multi-agent observation if ... Goal: Each agent's goal is to learn theta^* while minimizing fairness regret (Definition 1); albeit ensuring differential privacy guarantees (Definition 2).

symbols.L_merit: Lipschitz constant of the merit functions f^i
symbols.gamma_merit: minimum merit lower bound gamma on f^i
symbols.beta_T: confidence radius squared, max over agents of beta_t^i (at round T)

conditions: merit functions have minimum merit gamma > 0 and are L-Lipschitz
theta* lies in the confidence regions (choice of beta_t)
tuning: communication doubling until ceil(T/(m d^2 log^2(1+T/d))), then every ceil(T/(m d^2 log^2(1+T/d))) rounds

source.label: theorem: fairness regret
source.quote: With high probability, \algoname\ achieves a fairness regret of  O(\frac{4\nu L\sqrt{\beta_{t}}}{\gamma}\sqrt{mTd\log{(1+\frac{T}{d})} + m^{2}d^{3}\log^{3}{(1+\frac{T}{d})}}) when ||x_t^i(a)||_2 \leq 1 \forall a,t,i.

results.notes: Fairness regret is averaged over m agents (1/m sum), as defined; m (agents) mapped to N. Quantity is fairness regret (L1 policy distance), recorded as 'other'. Theorem writes beta_t but proof uses beta_T. Paper remarks that with beta_t = O(d log((1+mt)/alpha)) (Abbasi-Yadkori) this gives O~(d sqrt(mT log^2(1+mT/d))). Restated as Theorem 3 in appendix.

symbols.L_merit: Lipschitz constant of the merit functions
symbols.beta_T: confidence radius squared from Lemma 4 at round T
symbols.rho_bar: upper accuracy bound on privatizer noise matrices (Dubey & Pentland)
symbols.rho_low: lower accuracy bound on privatizer noise matrices

conditions: merit functions have minimum merit gamma and Lipschitz constant L
tuning: sqrt(beta_t^i) = sigma sqrt(2 log(2/alpha) + d log(rho_bar/rho_low + t/(d rho_low))) + m c sqrt(rho_bar) + m z

source.label: theorem: private fairness regret
source.quote: With high probability,  when ||x_t^i(a)||_2 \leq 1 \forall a,t,i and Lemma~\ref{lemma:beta_potential} holds, \ourprivalgo\ achieves a fairness regret of O(\frac{4\nu L\sqrt{\beta_{T}}}{\gamma}\sqrt{mTd\log{(\frac{\bar{\rho}}{\underline{\rho}} + \frac{T}{d\underline{\rho}})} + m^{2}d^{3}\log^{3}{(...)}}).

results.notes: Agent count m mapped to N. Fairness regret averaged over agents; recorded as 'other'. Privacy guarantee (Claim 1) not a regret bound. Restated as Theorem 4 in appendix.
